title: Rounds until a halted run satisfies a property
statement: Let $M$ be a nondeterministic Turing machine with $k$ work tapes, Boolean input, and state set $S$. Let $R$ be a natural number, and let $P$ and $	ext{Ready}$ be properties of configurations on a fixed Boolean input. Suppose that from every ready configuration, every choice word of length $R$ leads either to a halted configuration satisfying $P$, or to another ready configuration. Suppose also that every ready configuration is nonhalted. Then, for every natural number $j$, every ready initial configuration, and every choice word of length $Rj$, if the resulting run is halted, its final configuration satisfies $P$.
hypotheses_covered: A natural number of work tapes and a state set with decidable equality.
A fixed Boolean input and a nondeterministic machine on it.
Properties Ready and P of configurations, and a natural number R.
Every length-R choice word from a ready configuration ends halted with P, or ends ready.
A natural number j and a ready starting configuration.
A choice word of length R times j.
